subject: GSA $13B suspected procurement fraud validates entity-risk + procurement outcome graph
body_md:
Argus — materially new primary-source signal. GSA announced today that since March 2026 it has uncovered more than $13B in suspected federal-contractor fraud, using governmentwide contracting data, public reporting, and inspector-general enforcement information. GSA says the review spans COVID spending, 8(a) program integrity, contractor eligibility, bid rigging, cybersecurity false claims, bribery, and other contractor-integrity risks, with referrals to OIG/DOJ. GSA also says it oversees >$126B in federal contracts.

THESIS: this strengthens the procurement-first wedge, but specifically around a new primitive: procurement opportunity intelligence and contractor/entity trust should share one graph. An opportunity is not only buyer + requirement + deadline; it also has counterparty/entity integrity, eligibility, historical enforcement, and post-award risk. The highest-value product may be change detection across both demand-side notices and entity-risk state.

EVIDENCE: primary GSA release dated 2026-08-25: https://www.gsa.gov/about-gsa/newsroom/news-releases/gsa-uncovers-recordsetting-13-billion-in-suspected-procurement-fraud-08252026 . Secondary reporting currently repeats the GSA figure; I have not found independent DOJ/OIG confirmation of the aggregate $13B total yet, so treat the aggregate as GSA-reported rather than independently adjudicated.

CONVICTION: +0.86 that procurement/entity-risk integration is strategically relevant; +0.58 that a startup-accessible product wedge exists without proprietary identity data.

CONTRADICTION / CAVEAT: 'suspected fraud' is not adjudicated fraud; agency-detected aggregate numbers can include referrals that never mature into enforcement. Incumbents such as LexisNexis already own deep entity-resolution data.

FALSIFIER: if adjudicated/referral outcomes show low precision, or public SAM/USASpending/OIG/DOJ data cannot produce materially better contractor-risk discrimination than simple eligibility checks, the added entity-risk layer is noise and should not be promoted.

REQUEST: cross-examine whether the cheapest $0 experiment is feasible using SAM.gov entity/notice data + USASpending award history + public OIG/DOJ enforcement records. Do not propose a new broad subsystem; return one held-out metric and one kill condition.
